chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Muhammad ibn Asbagh, from Marwan ibn Muslim, from Burayd al-Ijli who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) so he said to me: If you had arrived a little earlier, you would have met Hayyan al-Sarraj. He said: And he pointed to a place in the room and said: He was sitting here. Then he mentioned Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya and talked about his life (continued existence) and began praising him and extolling him. So I said to him: O Hayyan! Do you not claim and others claim, and you narrate and others narrate: 'There was nothing in the Children of Israel except that it is also in this Umma like it'? He said: Yes. So I said: Then have we seen or you seen, or have we heard or you heard of a Scholar who died in the estimation of the people, and his wives were married off and his wealth was distributed, while he was alive and did not die? So he stood up and did not answer me anything.

key_terms.حَيَّانَ السَّرَّاجُ: Hayyan al-Sarraj, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.مَاتَ عَلَى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ: Died in the estimation of the people
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْحَنَفِيَّةِ: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya, son of Imam Ali

ai.seo_question: What is the evidence for the continued existence of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) engages Hayyan al-Sarraj in a dialectical discussion on the doctrine of *al-Hayat al-Khulud* (eternal life) of the Imams, using the precedent of Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya. He challenges the literalist interpretation of the maxim that 'what happened to the Children of Israel will happen to this Umma' by presenting a logical paradox: if a scholar dies visibly, his estate is distributed and his wives marry others, yet he remains alive, it proves that physical death is not the end of existence. This hadith serves as a foundational proof for the Shia belief in the occultation and continued physical/spiritual life of the Imams.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/152] Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh from al-Hasan b. Musa from Muhammad b. Asbagh from Marwan b. Muslim from Burayd al-Ijli who said:

I entered upon Abi Abdillah عليه السلام so he said to me: if you had come in a little earlier you would have met Hayyan al-Sarraj, he (Burayd) said: and he (al-Sadiq) pointed out a place in the room and said – he (Hayyan) was sat there, then he (Hayyan) brought up Muhammad b. al-Hanafiyya and talked about his life (continued existence), and he began praising him and extolling him. So I (al-Sadiq) said to him: O Hayyan! don’t you and others claim and narrate: ‘there is nothing that happened to the Bani Israil except that it is also to occur in this Umma’, he (Hayyan) replied: yes, so I (al-Sadiq) said: then have we or you seen or heard – a Scholar (divine leader) – who died in the estimation of the people (as far as the people were concerned), and his wives were married off, and his inheritance was redistributed, while he was still alive not dead?!, so he (Hayyan) stood up (to leave) and did not answer me anything.
